input.reasoning:
Backlog totals 210 story points across 24 tasks. With only one placeholder role ("Team member", 1 FTE, $75/hr) staffed on the project, all work must be sequenced through a single full-time person. Using a standard planning heuristic of ~6-8 hours of effort per story point (accounting for analysis, dev, testing, review, and coordination overhead for a single generalist doing everything), 210 points ≈ 1,470 hours at the midpoint (7 hrs/point). At 1 FTE (40 hrs/week), that is roughly 37 weeks (~8.5 months) of continuous work, before any vacation, illness, meetings, or context-switching overhead — which is itself a major delivery risk given the single-person capacity.

I have converted story points to hours using 7 hours/point as a central estimate (Likely scenario), 5.5 hours/point for an optimistic Best Case, and 9 hours/point for a pessimistic Worst Case, reflecting uncertainty in a single-generalist team tackling integration-heavy work (payments, legacy migration, RBAC).

Because there is only one role in the rate card, all labour is billed under "Team member" at $75/hr. I have not invented additional roles (e.g., QA, PM, DevOps) since the rate card explicitly restricts us to the one placeholder role. I flag in assumptions that this severely understates real-world cost and risk, since specialist work (payment integration, data migration, accessibility, security) normally requires distinct skillsets and would benefit from a proper multi-role team.

Non-labour costs are estimated for typical SaaS/infra costs a customer portal of this scope would incur: staging/production cloud hosting, Stripe integration/testing fees, third-party tooling (email service, search, monitoring), and a contingency for legacy data migration tooling license/support. These are indicative placeholders given no vendor quotes were supplied.

Priority breakdown reflects labour hours × $75, split proportionally by story points within each priority band (Urgent, High, Medium, Low), applied to the Likely-case total hours.

Reductions identify concrete descoping/deferral opportunities: dropping or deferring Low-priority items (support ticket sync, admin back-office, usage analytics, contract tests, legacy decommission) which total 39 points (~18% of backlog), deferring multi-currency support (13 points) to a post-launch phase, and trimming non-labour spend by deferring premium observability tooling until after initial launch.

assumptions: The rate card is a placeholder — only one generic role ('Team member', $75/hr, 1 FTE) exists; no real team roles or rates have been assigned yet, so this estimate is indicative only and should be revisited once actual roles (e.g., dev, QA, PM, DevOps) and rates are defined.
No historical actuals or real spend data exist for this project; all effort figures are derived from story-point heuristics rather than observed velocity.

Story points converted to hours at 7 hrs/point (Likely), 5.5 hrs/point (Best Case), and 9 hrs/point (Worst Case) to reflect uncertainty for a single generalist covering analysis, build, test and review for all 24 tasks.

With only 1 FTE available, the 210-point backlog implies ~37 weeks (about 8.5 months) of continuous solo work at the Likely-case estimate, with no allowance for leave, meetings, or context-switching — this is a significant delivery risk and the role is staffed far too thinly for the backlog it must absorb.
Non-labour costs (hosting, Stripe fees, email/search/monitoring subscriptions, migration tooling) are indicative estimates based on typical SaaS project costs, since no vendor quotes were supplied.
Priority-based cost breakdown is computed by allocating the Likely-case total hours proportionally to each task's story points, grouped by priority band.

Legacy data migration (PW-8, 21 points) and payment integration (PW-7, 13 points) are treated as high-complexity/high-risk items; their true cost could exceed this estimate materially if specialist skills are not available on the single staffed role.
All 24 backlog items are assumed in-scope for this estimate; reductions below identify candidates for descoping or deferral to lower cost.

reductions.description: Descope or defer all Low-priority items (PW-12 Support ticket submission, PW-18 Admin back-office, PW-19 Usage analytics, PW-23 Contract tests, PW-24 Decommission legacy portal — 39 points total) to a later phase.
reductions.effect: Removes ~39 of 210 story points (~18.5%) from the current phase, reducing Likely-case labour hours by roughly 273 hours at $75/hr.

reductions.description: Defer Multi-currency support (PW-14, 13 points) until after initial launch, since single-currency (USD) launch is viable for an initial customer base.
reductions.effect: Removes 13 points (~91 hours at 7 hrs/point) from the current phase.

reductions.description: Defer Usage analytics and reporting (PW-19) and Admin back-office (PW-18) specifically if not already covered by the Low-priority group above; combine with a lighter-weight interim support workflow instead of full admin tooling.
reductions.effect: Removes 21 points (~147 hours) if implemented independently of the Low-priority bundle above; apply only one of these two reductions to avoid double-counting.

reductions.description: Reduce non-labour spend by deferring premium observability tooling (tracing/dashboards) and using free-tier/open-source alternatives until post-launch scale requires it.
reductions.effect: Cuts the Observability non-labour line from $1,500 to a minimal $300 free-tier footprint.

reductions.description: Negotiate or delay legacy data migration tooling licensing (PW-8) by running migration in-house with existing scripts rather than paid tooling, if feasible.
reductions.effect: Removes the one-off $3,000 migration tooling/support non-labour line entirely.
